items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I think Noble Sissel got -- in fact, all of them made more money than we made

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Louis Russell and Benny Carter and groups like that?

If I know the people who owned that place, they didn't pay the band that kind of money. That was the kind of money they paid for the shows. That was the kind of money they paid for the shows, and I'll tell you, I think Noble Sissel got -- in fact, all of them made more money than we made, because it seems like when you play at a place a long time, the booking agents were able to bring in acts -- when they get through romancing an owner of an establishment, the booking agents are able to talk and get more money…
To the best of my knowledge, they paid the bands that came in there much more money than they paid us. But whether they paid them $4,000 a week, that, I don't know.
